description: Use for "interrogate", "adversarial review", "multi-model review", "challenge this", "stress test this code", "find blind spots", or "tear this apart". Adversaries try to break a change or design, and only findings proven by a run survive.

compare.without: Pads the list with style and naming opinions.
compare.with: Gives each finding with the command, its actual output, and the expected output.

compare.without: Accepts whatever a reviewer claims is broken.
compare.with: Reruns every finding's command and drops any that don't show the failure.

compare.without: Fixes the code as soon as it spots a problem.
compare.with: Hands back a report only. You decide what to fix.

brief.intro: It says adversaries try to break the change, only findings proven by a run count, and it reports without fixing.
sections: Defaults to the whole branch diff, restates the intent with `in-your-own-words`, and asks you when the intent is unclear.
Reuses `arena`'s spawning steps, giving each adversary its own worktree and the same "break this change" brief.
Reruns each finding's command, keeps it only if it fails and breaks the intent, and merges shared root causes.
Reports three parts: the restated intent, each verified finding with who found it, and each adversary's dropped count and reasons.

lessons.quote: Adversaries try to break a change or a design.
lessons.quoteTr: Adversaries try to break a change or a design.
lessons.title: Cast the AI as an opponent
lessons.does: The helpers aren't there to vouch for the code. Their job is to break it.
lessons.why: "Adversary" and "break" turn "take a look" into "defeat it", so the AI hunts harder.
lessons.try: When the AI reviews a plan, say: "You're the toughest competitor. Prove this plan won't work."

lessons.quote: Report each finding with a title, the exact command, the output it printed, and the output the intent requires.
lessons.quoteTr: Report each finding with a title, the exact command, the output it printed, and the output the intent requires.
lessons.title: Put actual next to expected
lessons.does: Each problem comes with the command, what it printed, and what it should print, so you can rerun it.
lessons.why: Writing "what happened" next to "what should happen" shows the gap at once and leaves no room for hand-waving.
lessons.try: When the AI reports bugs, write: "For each: what you did, what you saw, what you expected to see."

lessons.quote: Leave out anything you did not run. That covers style, naming, structure, and risks that need a future change to matter.
lessons.quoteTr: Leave out anything you did not run. That covers style, naming, structure, and risks that need a future change to matter.
lessons.title: Name what the rule covers
lessons.does: It won't pad the list with naming, style, or "might break later". Every finding was actually run.
lessons.why: "Leave out what you didn't run" leaves gaps. Naming the kinds most likely to sneak in closes them.
lessons.try: When the AI hunts for problems, write: "Only report what stops a customer paying. Colors, wording, and future risks don't count."

lessons.quote: No findings is a valid result.
lessons.quoteTr: No findings is a valid result.
lessons.title: Say "nothing" is a fine answer
lessons.does: When the code is fine, it says so instead of inventing problems to look busy.
lessons.why: An AI asked to find problems feels it must find some. Saying an empty result counts removes that pressure.
lessons.try: When the AI checks your work, add: "If you find no typos, just reply 'none found'."

blocks: Adversaries try to break a change or a design. A finding survives only when a run proves it. Report the findings. Do not apply fixes.

The scope is what the user names. Otherwise it is the branch diff from its merge base with the base branch, through the working tree. State the intent with the **in-your-own-words** skill, from the user's message, the commits, and the PR description. Ask the user when the intent is unclear.

Run Phase A steps 3 and 4 and Phase B of the **arena** skill, with four changes. Read the `interrogate reviewers` line in place of `arena runners`. Copy the scope's uncommitted changes into each worktree. Spawn each adversary as a general-purpose subagent (`generalPurpose` in Cursor). In place of the arena task and rationale, give each adversary the scope, the intent, and this brief:

> Break this change. Prove each finding with a run against the real code, such as a failing test, a repro script, or command output that shows the wrong behavior. For a design or plan, run a prototype or probe the current tree. Keep repros in your own worktree. Report each finding with a title, the exact command, the output it printed, and the output the intent requires. Leave out anything you did not run. That covers style, naming, structure, and risks that need a future change to matter. No findings is a valid result.

Verify each finding per arena Phase F by rerunning its command. Keep a finding when the output shows the failure and the failure breaks the intent. Drop the rest. Merge findings that share a root cause.
Skip arena Phases C, D, and E. Adversaries find different failures, so the verdict keeps every verified finding, not one adversary's list.

- **Intent**: the restatement.
- **Findings**: for each verified finding, the command, its output, how it breaks the intent, and the adversaries that found it. Say "no verified findings" when none survive.
- **Dropped**: for each adversary, the count of dropped findings and why.
